NCur (20 mg/kg) showed antidepressant-like effect in forced swimming test (P<0.001) and tail suspension test (P<0.05), anxiolytic-like effect in elevated plus maze (P<0.05) and open filed test (P<0.01), and improved the memory and cognition in passive avoidance test (P<0.05), but Cur (20 mg/kg) had no effect. Histopathology results showed that NCur (5 mg/kg) led to optimal neuronal survival in CA1, improved cellular organization in CA3, and the highest count of normal neurons in the dentate gyrus. NCur demonstrated potential to treat the depressive/anxiety-like behaviors and impaired cognition induced by the PWSI model in male mice. Histopathological data also showed improvements in hippocampal regions.

articles.title: Survivin mRNA-lipid nanoparticles promote activation of CD8+Granzyme B+ T cells and effector memory formation for effective oral cancer immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Effective cancer immunotherapy requires an understanding of the tumor microenvironment (TME) to overcome immune suppression and provide a durable anti-tumor response. Here, we present preclinical evaluation of survivin antigen-encoded mRNA lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) in a murine oral cancer model. In vivo anti-tumor efficacy studies in early-stage tumors (induced by MOC1 cells, tumor volume ∼100 mm3) showed complete tumor elimination within 7-10 days after survivin mRNA-LNPs administration. The mechanistic studies performed to analyze immune cell (including dendritic cells and T cells) activation using flow cytometry and complementary cytokine profiling by ELISA revealed immune reprogramming. Survivin mRNA-LNP administration showed a broad, multi-compartmental T-cell immune response compared with control group. The treatment group showed significantly greater CD4+ and CD8+ T cell expansion in lymph nodes by day 3 (p<0.0001) and robust infiltration into the TME by day 14 (p<0.001) compared with control group. The survivin mRNA-LNPs promoted T cell activation (CD69+, CD28+) and increased cytotoxic CD8+Granzyme B+ T cells in the TME (p<0.001). The survivin mRNA-LNPs group showed controlled Treg levels in the TME providing a favorable effector to Treg ratio critical for superior anti-tumor efficacy. Furthermore, tumor rechallenge study showed formation of immunological memory against oral cancer cells. In conclusion, the present study provides a mechanistic understanding of survivin mRNA-LNP-mediated immune modulation in oral cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetic modeling of idarubicin and idarubicinol in Acute Myeloid Leukemia induction therapy: An Ancillary Study of the BIG-1 Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Idarubicin, a key anthracycline used in the induction treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), is characterized by large interindividual pharmacokinetic (PK) variability. This variability may impact both efficacy and toxicity, highlighting the need for a better understanding of exposure variability and its determinants. METHODS: A joint population PK model of idarubicin and its active metabolite idarubicinol was developed using data from 27 patients enrolled in the BIG-1 study. Plasma concentrations were measured on day 1 of induction therapy following intravenous idarubicin administration. Idarubicin and idarubicinol were quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with fluorescence detection. Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling was used to describe concentration-time profiles and explore associations with clinical and biological covariates. RESULTS: Among the structures evaluated, a three-compartment model for idarubicin coupled with a two-compartment model for idarubicinol provided the best fit to the observed concentration-time data within 24 hours following infusion. Body surface area and baseline lymphocyte count were identified as exploratory covariates associated with peripheral distribution volumes. CONCLUSIONS: This study describes idarubicin and idarubicinol concentration-time profiles over the observed 24-hour period in patients receiving AML induction therapy. Associations with body surface area and lymphocyte count require confirmation in an independent population. These findings provide a pharmacometric basis for future exposure-response investigations and prospective evaluation of model-informed therapeutic strategies approaches in AML.

articles.title: Serum Concentration Relationships of Candesartan in Migraine Prevention.
articles.abstract: Migraine is a common disabling disorder, and optimising affordable preventive treatments remains highly relevant. Candesartan is an effective and well-tolerated preventive treatment, but little is known about its dose-concentration-response relationships. We explored these relationships using data from the MigriNor study, a prospective observational cohort of adults with episodic or chronic migraine initiating oral preventive treatment. A total of 166 participants using candesartan were included (median age 35 years; 89% female). Participants completed a daily electronic headache diary during a 4-week baseline and 12-week follow-up period with accompanying blood sampling. Dosing regimen was flexible. No differences in adverse drug reactions (ADRs) or treatment acceptability were observed between participants starting 4 versus 8 mg. Substantial interindividual variability in serum concentrations was observed. Higher serum concentrations were associated with lower odds of headache attacks (OR = 0.97, 95% CI = 0.96-0.98, p < 0.001) and migraine attacks (OR = 0.98, 95% CI = 0.97-0.99, p = 0.005). Interquartile ranges of serum concentrations among ≥ 30% and ≥ 50% responders were 62.9-141.2 and 62.3-129.3 nmol/L, respectively, suggesting preliminary therapeutic reference ranges. Serum concentration was not associated with ADRs or treatment acceptability. Interpretation is limited by the flexible dosing design, and studies with fixed dosing regimens are warranted.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profile of high-dose D9-tetrahydrocannabinol in male and female rats.
articles.abstract: Cannabis products with elevated Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content are prevalent in parts of North America, yet their pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) properties remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the effects of a single administration of high-dose THC (10 and 30 mg/kg, intraperitoneal, IP) compared with a lower dose (3 mg/kg, IP) in male and female Long Evans rats. Plasma, brain, and white adipose tissue concentrations of THC and its metabolites 11-hydroxy-THC and 11-carboxy-THC were quantified over acute (up to 24 h) and prolonged (14 days) periods. Behavioral endpoints included ingestive behavior, pica, locomotor activity, anxiety-like and stress-coping responses, and nociception. Plasma concentrations of multiple cytokines were also assessed. PK results showed nonlinear disposition with disproportionate increases in maximal concentration at higher doses, greater systemic and tissue exposure in females, and extensive sequestration in adipose tissue. PD effects were also dose- and sex-dependent: suppression of food/water intake and body weight, transient locomotor stimulation in females at low dose and suppression at high doses, increased pica in females at 30 mg/kg, modest anxiety-like shifts, bidirectional stress-coping changes in males, and antinociception primarily in males at 1 hour and 24 hours postdosing. No meaningful changes in proinflammatory or anti-inflammatory cytokines were observed in either sex. The findings indicate that high-dose THC produces nonlinear sex-dependent PK with prolonged central and peripheral retention, alongside distinct acute PD profiles compared with lower doses. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: High-potency cannabis products are common, yet their impact on health remains poorly understood. This study shows that high-dose THC produces nonlinear, sex-dependent distribution and metabolism in rats, with females showing markedly greater systemic exposure, prolonged brain retention, and extensive adipose sequestration, alongside distinct acute pharmacological profiles. These findings show that high-dose THC generates disproportionate systemic and central exposure and distinct acute pharmacological profiles compared with lower doses.

articles.title: Comparison of monosodium iodoacetate, medial meniscal transection, and partial medial meniscectomy in vivo rat models of osteoarthritis from the pain and industrial perspective.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a major global health burden marked by progressive cartilage degeneration and chronic pain with intertwined inflammatory and neuropathic mechanisms. This study compared three rat OA models, monosodium iodoacetate (MIA), medial meniscal transection (MMT), and partial medial meniscectomy (MNX), to assess their translational value, suitability for pharmaceutical research, and identify the most robust and reproducible model for preclinical OA pain research. OA was induced in male Wistar (MIA) or Sprague Dawley (MMT, MNX) rats, and pain progression was evaluated by testing mechanical sensitivity and dynamic weight-bearing. A single oral dose of pregabalin (30 mg/kg) was used for pharmacological validation. The MIA model produced a rapid, robust pain phenotype, with pronounced mechanical hypersensitivity and consistent weight-bearing deficits by day 21. Surgical models progressed more slowly and variably: hypersensitivity emerged by day 21 in MNX rats and by day 49 in MMT rats. Neither surgical model generated stable dynamic weight-bearing deficits, indicating limited sensitivity of current gait-analysis methods for detecting their subtler impairments. Pregabalin reduced mechanical hypersensitivity across all 3 models, confirming their pharmacological validity and utility for analgesic screening. Overall, the MIA model remains the most efficient and reliable for industrial research due to its strong behavioral window, whereas the MNX model offers greater translational relevance if paired with more sensitive and objective behavioral measures. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: By systematically comparing chemical and surgical rat models of osteoarthritis, this study clarifies their strengths and limitations for modeling chronic pain. The results demonstrate that, although the monosodium iodoacetate model delivers robust, reproducible behavioral outcomes, surgical models more accurately reflect disease progression but lack sensitive behavioral readouts. This work informs translational model selection and underscores the need for more objective pain assessment tools.

articles.title: Structurome-wide analysis reveals intracellular loop 2 folding as an activation-associated feature of class A G protein-coupled receptors.
articles.abstract: Activation of class A G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) is commonly described through rearrangement of the transmembrane-bundle and engagement of the Gα α5 helix, whereas the conformational behavior of intracellular loop 2 (ICL2) has not been examined systematically across the structural record. Here, I classified ICL2 as folded, unfolded, or disordered in 1358 experimental class A GPCR structures using a backbone-dihedral criterion and evaluated the classification against activation state, transducer class, crystallization fusions, ICL2-proximal modulators, and resolution. The assignment was additionally assessed using Dictionary of Secondary-Structure of Proteins and a literature-anchored benchmark set. In canonical fusion-free structures, ICL2 was folded in 84% of active structures compared with 53% of inactive structures [odds ratio, 4.74; two-sided Fisher exact test; descriptive P = 7 × 10-13]. The association remained evident after controlling for receptor overrepresentation, within receptors represented in both states, and among active structures without an annotated transducer. Crystallization fusions were associated with increased apparent ICL2 folding in inactive structures. Folded and unfolded ICL2 also showed distinct Gα contact patterns, while sequence features displayed only modest associations with folding. A geometrically compatible contact between ICL2 position 34.53 and the conserved D3.49 residue accompanied the folded state but was not universal. These exploratory structural analyses identify ICL2 folding as an activation-associated feature of class A GPCRs without establishing a causal mechanism or a determinant of transducer selectivity. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This structure-wide analysis shows that intracellular loop 2 (ICL2) folding is strongly enriched in active compared with inactive class A GPCR structures, identifying ICL2 as an intracellular structural readout of receptor activation. The association is retained across major structural controls, while transducer analyses show that ICL2 folding is most prevalent in Gs-bound complexes but does not by itself define coupling specificity.

articles.title: Dual targeting of cytochrome bd and bc1-aa3 terminal oxidases eradicates phenotypically diverse population of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
articles.abstract: Bedaquiline approval paved the way for the development of drug candidates against energy metabolism pathways of TB-causing organisms, and oxidative phosphorylation was proven to be a relevant target domain. While bedaquiline acts on the F1F0 ATP synthase, Q203 targets the cytochrome bc1-aa3 terminal oxidase, which mediates electron transport to O2 in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. However, due to functional redundancies between cytochrome bc1-aa3 and a second terminal oxidase, the cytochrome-bd, the sterilization effect of Q203 is impaired. Here, we describe the identification of BD-2, a novel small molecule inhibitor of the cytochrome-bd in a cell-based screening campaign. Alone, BD-2 does not exhibit any significant activity. When paired with Q203, however, BD-2 strongly inhibits Mycobacterium tuberculosis respiratory chain function and ATP synthesis. Moreover, BD-2 combined with Q203 was shown to possess potent bactericidal effect on both replicating and nonreplicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including those living under nutrient starved and hypoxic conditions, representing the persistent forms found in granulomas of patients. Mechanistic analysis included molecular docking studies using the known structure of Mycobacterium tuberculosis cytochrome-bd, in vitro activity testing on purified enzyme, all of which confirmed that BD-2 is a direct cytochrome-bd inhibitor. Furthermore, the BD-2/Q203 combination was effective against intracellular bacteria in an in vitro macrophage infection model based on THP-1 cells, with over 90% reduction in bacterial load achieved at clinically relevant concentrations. This study supports the hypothesis of combining a cytochrome-bd inhibitor and Q203 in tuberculosis therapy as a rational, mechanistically driven approach that might result in more efficient treatment and overcome antibiotic tolerance.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Cardioprotective role of GTS-21 by attenuating the TLR4/NF-κB pathway in streptozotocin-induced diabetic cardiomyopathy in rats.
Association of 24-hours net positive fluid balance with log-transformed vancomycin trough concentrations in the early phase of therapy among critically ill patients.
articles.abstract: Early vancomycin troughs are frequently low in critical illness and fluid accumulation may contribute through distribution effects. This study estimated the association between net positive fluid balance and early vancomycin troughs as a hypothesis-generating analysis and explored variation across early-therapy windows and by hypoalbuminemia. A retrospective cohort study used ICU electronic health record data from MIMIC-IV. ICU stays with a timing-validated trough were included. The primary cohort N = 255 required at least 80% EMAR dose capture in the prior 24 h and delta serum creatinine at or below 0.2 mg/dL across the 48 h before trough and trough within 72 h of first IV dose. Net fluid balance in the prior 24 h was modeled per + 5 L. Outcome was log trough. Models adjusted for serum creatinine and administered dose and administration count in the prior 24 h. Sensitivity windows were within 48 h (N = 162) and within 96 h (N = 289). Hypoalbuminemia below 3 g/dL was explored in the measured subset. Median trough was 14.00 mg/L (IQR 10.15 to 18.15) and 62 of 255 were below 10 mg/L (24.3%). The point estimate suggested an 11.7% lower trough concentration per + 5 L net positive balance (β =  - 0.1247; SE = 0.079; p = 0.115), but the 95% CI (- 24.4% to + 3.1%) included no association. Serum creatinine had a positive coefficient (β = 0.2995; p = 0.061). Point estimates were similar across early-therapy windows with all confidence intervals including no association. The exploratory albumin interaction was imprecise and limited by substantial missingness and small subgroup sizes. The point estimate suggested lower early vancomycin troughs with higher net positive fluid balance, but the confidence interval included no association. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation to clarify whether fluid balance is associated with early trough concentrations and area under the curve exposure.

articles.title: 'Harmful' or 'excipients of concern'? Rethinking terminology and risk in pediatric excipients.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Excipients, though often overshadowed by active pharmaceutical ingredients, are essential for the successful formulation of medicinal products. They serve critical roles, such as enhancing drug stability, ensuring proper delivery, and facilitating patient compliance. However, the perception of excipients has become increasingly polarized, with some being labeled as 'Harmful' or 'Dangerous' without a thorough and balanced analysis of contributing factors. AREAS COVERED: This commentary seeks to address this growing concern. A targeted PubMed and Embase literature search was conducted for relevant publications that categorize excipients as dangerous, often without consideration of contextual factors like patient age group, dosage form, disease severity, and exposure levels to the excipients in question. This blanket labeling, instead of providing a well-rounded analysis of risk-versus-benefit and safety data for the pediatric population, may spread fear rather than help clinicians make informed decisions. By analyzing the methodologies and assumptions underlying these studies, this commentary highlights the gaps and biases that may lead to miscommunication and unwarranted fear in the healthcare community. EXPERT OPINION: Shifting from terms such as 'harmful,' 'hazardous,' or 'dangerous' to 'excipients of concern' reflects a more balanced, evidence-based approach. It recognizes the complexities of excipient use, enabling informed decisions prioritizing safety and efficacy.

articles.title: Mechanisms of XCR1 Membrane Trafficking and Constitutive Endocytosis.
articles.abstract: Chemokines orchestrate immune cell trafficking through receptor-mediated signalling and are implicated in inflammatory, autoimmune and neuropathic disorders. The XCL1-XCR1 axis is of particular interest because XCR1 is selectively expressed on mature conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s), where it supports communication with activated CD8+ T cells and NK cells and promotes antigen cross-presentation. This selectivity has made XCR1 an attractive target for dendritic cell-based cancer vaccines, while emerging evidence also links XCL1-XCR1 signalling to neuroinflammation and pain. Despite its therapeutic potential, the mechanisms governing XCR1 activation and trafficking remain understudied. Here, we characterize XCR1 expression, membrane trafficking, and basal internalization to define mechanisms that may influence therapeutic targeting. We show that XCR1 undergoes constitutive internalization through a β-arrestin-independent but adaptor protein 2 (AP2)-dependent pathway, distinguishing it from other chemokine receptors with constitutive endocytosis. Furthermore, we identify specific sequence motifs critical for its subcellular localization and intracellular trafficking. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into XCR1 regulation and may inform the development of targeted therapeutics and antigen-delivery strategies in cancer and inflammation.

articles.title: Cefepime-Zidebactam: Leveraging β-Lactam Enhancement Against Difficult-to-Treat and Metallo-β-Lactamase-Producing Gram-Negative Pathogens.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem resistance among Gram-negative bacteria remains a serious public health threat, with metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing organisms increasing substantially in prevalence and few therapeutic options available to adequately address these difficult-to-treat pathogens. Cefepime-zidebactam (FEP-ZID) is a novel β-lactam/β-lactam enhancer combination that offers a mechanistically distinct approach to overcoming resistance in Gram-negative organisms. Zidebactam contributes three complementary mechanisms: inhibition of Class A and C β-lactamases, direct antibacterial activity via PBP2 inhibition, and enhancement of cefepime activity through a reduction in the pharmacodynamic exposure required for bactericidal effect, allowing FEP-ZID to achieve substantial reductions in bacterial burden even in isolates with elevated minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). FEP-ZID was recently approved in the United States for the treatment of complicated urinary tract infection (cUTI), including acute pyelonephritis, caused by Enterobacterales and/or Pseudomonas aeruginosa. FEP-ZID demonstrates broad in vitro and in vivo activity against isolates producing Class A, B, C, and D β-lactamases, as well as organisms harboring PBP3 alterations that are otherwise associated with reduced susceptibility to currently available MBL-active therapies. This spectrum extends across carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, P. aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii, and includes activity against isolates with porin loss and efflux upregulation, resistance mechanisms that commonly limit the utility of other β-lactam-based agents. In vivo infection models utilizing humanized regimens have demonstrated bactericidal activity against isolates with FEP-ZID MICs up to 64 μg/mL. The Phase 3 ENHANCE I trial demonstrated noninferiority and subsequent superiority over meropenem in cUTI (including acute pyelonephritis), driven primarily by microbiological response, with favorable outcomes observed across many baseline pathogens, including extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing isolates and patients with concomitant bacteremia. Compassionate use experience further suggests possible utility in severe multidrug-resistant infections across multiple infection types, including bloodstream, osteoarticular, and intra-abdominal infections caused by MBL-producing organisms. Collectively, available preclinical and clinical evidence positions FEP-ZID as a mechanistically distinct option for difficult-to-treat Gram-negative infections, with additional clinical study needed to define its role beyond the currently approved indication.

articles.title: Linking preclinical models with functional imaging and artificial intelligence to decode tumor angiogenesis.
articles.abstract: Tumor angiogenesis is a hallmark of cancer, influencing oxygen delivery, immune cell trafficking, and therapeutic response. Although anti-angiogenic therapies have achieved clinical relevance, their efficacy remains limited by tumor heterogeneity, adaptive resistance, and insufficient functional assessment of tumor vasculature. In this review, we evaluate preclinical models of tumor angiogenesis with a focus on their ability to generate quantitative and physiologically relevant readouts. We discuss established assays such as tube formation, fibrin bead assay, aortic ring, and chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) models, alongside emerging systems including vascularized organoids and organ-on-a-chip platforms, as well as zebrafish and murine tumor models. Particular emphasis is placed on advanced imaging modalities enabling longitudinal assessment of perfusion, permeability, and vascular remodeling, as well as on the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in automated and quantitative data interpretation. We further highlight the integration of single-cell and multi-omics approaches for resolving endothelial heterogeneity and tumor-stroma interactions. By linking biologically relevant models with functional imaging and computational analysis, this review outlines strategies to improve the predictive power and translational relevance of angiogenesis research.

articles.title: Dietary Acrylamide-Glycidamide Exposure and Metabolic Toxicity: Emerging Evidence in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Acrylamide is present in a variety of cooked and processed foods, but its precise role in the biological mechanisms underlying type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains incompletely understood. This review aimed to comprehensively evaluate the relationship between dietary acrylamide exposure, T2D-related metabolic dysfunction, and the molecular mechanisms responsible for its adverse effects. METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted by searching PubMed®, ScienceDirect®, Google Scholar®, and MEDLINE® for English-language publications published between 2002 and 2025. The search strategy used the following Boolean search string: ("acrylamide" OR "glycidamide") AND ("diabetes" OR "type 2 diabetes" OR "insulin resistance" OR "β-cell dysfunction") AND ("oxidative stress" OR "glucose metabolism"). More than 100 relevant publications were identified and included in this review. RESULTS: Current evidence suggests that dietary acrylamide exposure contributes to metabolic dysfunction through multiple interconnected mechanisms, including oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, glycation, insulin resistance, and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. Experimental and epidemiological studies indicate that acrylamide may impair glucose metabolism and insulin signalling, thereby contributing to the development and progression of T2D. However, the consistency of epidemiological evidence remains limited by methodological differences and potential confounding factors. DISCUSSION: The available evidence highlights the potential role of dietary acrylamide as a modifiable environmental risk factor for T2D. Strategies aimed at reducing dietary acrylamide exposure through improved food processing, cooking practices, and nutritional interventions may help mitigate metabolic risk. Nevertheless, further well-designed prospective studies and mechanistic investigations are needed to clarify the causal relationship and strengthen the current evidence base. CONCLUSION: Dietary acrylamide exposure may adversely affect glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, and pancreatic β-cell function, thereby contributing to the development and progression of T2D. Although current evidence supports a potential association, further high-quality clinical and epidemiological studies are required to establish causality and inform evidence-based preventive strategies.

articles.title: Medicinal Plants in the Management of Anxiety Disorders: Clinical Evidence, Mechanisms, and Safety Considerations.
articles.abstract: Anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent neuropsychiatric conditions worldwide and represent a major public health burden. Although conventional pharmacological treatments are effective, their long-term use is often limited by adverse effects, including sedation, dependence, and cognitive impairment, prompting growing interest in medicinal plants as alternative or adjunct therapies. This review summarizes current evidence on selected medicinal plants, including Bacopa monnieri, Crocus sativus, Withania somnifera, and Piper methysticum, with emphasis on their pharmacological mechanisms, therapeutic efficacy, and safety profiles in anxiety management. Preclinical and clinical studies suggest that these plants exert anxiolytic effects through modulation of neurotransmitter systems, particularly γ-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA), serotonin, and dopamine pathways, as well as regulation of the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis. In addition, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties may contribute to neuroprotection and improved stress resilience. Clinical findings indicate that certain herbal preparations may offer benefits comparable to conventional therapies for mild to moderate anxiety, often with fewer adverse effects. However, variability in study design, lack of standardized formulations, and insufficient long-term safety data remain significant limitations. Therefore, well-designed randomized controlled trials and mechanistic investigations are required to establish efficacy, safety, and standardization. Overall, medicinal plants show promising potential as complementary or alternative therapeutic options for anxiety disorders, provided their use is supported by rigorous scientific validation.

articles.title: Reply: Comparison of Train-of-Four Versus No Train-of-Four Monitoring of Neuromuscular Blockade on Drug Consumption for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
Lipid-based Nanocarriers for Atorvastatin Delivery: Current Developments and Clinical Translation Prospects.
articles.abstract: Atorvastatin is a well-established first-line medication for treating dyslipidemia, but has significant drawbacks of low aqueous solubility, extensive first-pass metabolism, and limited oral bioavailability. Over recent years, lipid-based nanocarriers have emerged as a viable platform to improve atorvastatin's pharmacokinetic profile by enhancing solubility, facilitating absorption via the lymphatic system, and providing a controlled drug release profile. This review provides a comprehensive overview of four primary lipid-based delivery systems: solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs), nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs), liposomes, and self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery systems (SNEDDS), and their specific application to atorvastatin. Each type of delivery system is reviewed in detail, including composition, drug loading and release mechanisms, encapsulation efficiency, physical characteristics (particle size, surface charge), and in vivo performance. Comparative evaluations indicate that NLCs and SNEDDS achieve the highest bioavailability enhancements (up to five-fold) via improved solubilization and lymphatic transport, whereas SLNs provide superior stability and controlled release, and liposomes offer versatile encapsulation yet limited shelf stability. Additionally, this review integrates current competitive patent opportunities, formulation optimization strategies, and translational research findings from both preclinical and clinical studies. Collectively, these findings show that thoughtful lipid-carrier design can significantly improve atorvastatin's pharmacokinetic profile and ultimately enable the development of large-scale, patient-focused oral lipid formulations.

articles.title: A Review on Mechanisms of Action and Signaling Pathways of Natural Anti-hyperpigmentation Agents.
articles.abstract: Hyperpigmentation is a dermatological condition characterized by excessive melanin production, resulting in skin darkening. Intrinsic and extrinsic mediators, including ultraviolet (UV) radiation, hormonal changes, inflammation, and genetic predisposition, contribute to hyperpigmentation pathogenesis. The current review thoroughly examines the biological processes involved in hyperpigmentation, with particular emphasis on its signaling pathways, particularly the cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP), wingless-related integration site (Wnt)/β-catenin, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt), and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), thereby providing mechanistic insights that may facilitate the development of effective treatments. The review also evaluates the safety, toxicity, and therapeutic efficacy of TYR inhibitors, arbutin, azelaic acid, ellagic acid, kojic acid, resveratrol, and the melanosome inhibitor niacinamide, for managing hyperpigmentation. Additionally, the review summarizes the in vitro and in vivo studies of these agents and other emerging plant extracts. Recent advances in the use of plant extracts for hyperpigmentation have shown promising efficacy; nevertheless, their translation into clinical and commercial applications remains limited. This limited translation might be attributed to the challenges related to standardization and the paucity of clinical evidence regarding long-term safety. Moreover, ongoing studies on natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents have highlighted the critical role of patent analyses in the advancement of biomedical research. This review provides a strategic direction for researchers to assess the safety, efficacy, and toxicity profiles of natural anti-hyperpigmentation agents.

articles.title: Cannabinoids for Acute Pain Management: A Contemporary Scoping Review of Evidence, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The global opioid crisis has intensified interest in non-opioid and opioid-sparing analgesic strategies, including cannabinoids. Despite the expanding legal landscape for cannabis and a rapidly growing cannabinoid market, the clinical evidence for cannabinoid use in acute pain management remains inconsistent and largely of low quality. METHODS: This contemporary scoping review was conducted and reported in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search of six electronic databases (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalKey, EMBASE, the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and BIOSIS) was performed for literature published between 1 January 2016 and 5 April 2026, with the final database search executed on 5 April 2026, addressing the pharmacology, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, and perioperative implications of cannabinoids in acute and postoperative pain. Two blinded reviewers independently screened records and charted data against predefined eligibility criteria; discrepancies were resolved by a third author. Findings are summarized narratively and in tabular format, and the study selection process is depicted in a PRISMA flow diagram. RESULTS: Preclinical evidence supports robust antinociceptive effects of cannabinoids through multiple receptor pathways; however, these findings have not translated reliably into human acute pain models. Metaanalytic data demonstrate either no significant reduction in acute pain scores with cannabinoids versus placebo, or only small, clinically uncertain improvements. The opioid-sparing effect, while promising in preclinical and some chronic pain studies, has not been demonstrated for acute postoperative pain. A notable exception is a 2024 randomized trial showing a 40% reduction in opioid requirements with perioperative dronabinol after cardiac surgery. Safety data indicate that non-serious adverse events (dizziness, nausea, sedation) are consistently more frequent with cannabinoids than placebo. The 2023 American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine (ASRA) consensus guidelines now formalize 21 recommendations for perioperative cannabinoid management. CONCLUSION: While the biological rationale for cannabinoid analgesia is compelling, the clinical evidence base for acute pain remains insufficient to support routine use. Cannabinoids may serve as adjuncts in specific populations, but require careful patient selection, dose titration, and safety monitoring. Well-designed, large randomized controlled trials targeting defined acute pain populations are urgently needed.

articles.title: Mechanistic attenuation by L-carnitine of trastuzumab-induced downregulation of adenosine monophosphate -activated protein kinase signal in cardiac H9c2 cells.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical usefulness of trastuzumab (TZ) is restrained owing to its cardiotoxic effect. This investigation was initiated to evaluate the potential protective impact of carnitine (CARN) against TZ-related cardiac influence; and to uncover the underlining mechanism. METHODS: Cytotoxic effect of TZ, CARN and their combination was assessed in cardiac H9c2 cells. Carnitine pamlitoyltransferase-1B (CPT1B) and adenosine monophosphate activated protein kinase-α2 (AMPK-α2) expression were investigated using quantitative real-time Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR). Troponin I, creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB), Adenosine triphosphate (ATP), malonyl-CoA, acetyl-CoA carboxylase-2 (ACC2) and autophagy protein 5 (ATG-5) were investigated using Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). RESULTS: Challenging cardiac cell with TZ resulted in concentration-dependent decrease in cell viability with inhibitory concentration 50 (IC50) of (1.21 uM). Combining TZ's IC50 and CARN (5 mM) resulted in the most profound drop of cardiac cellular toxicity. Trastuzumab elevated Troponin I, CK-MB, ACC-2 and Malonyl-CoA, while CARN counteracted this elevation. TZ decreased mRNA expression of AMPK-α2 and CPT1B; as well as ATP and ATG-5 levels, but combination of TZ and CARN counteracted this reduction. CONCLUSIONS: TZ disorders AMPK-α2 downstream signaling with the consequent decrease of ATP production and disturbs autophagy. Carnitine tempers TZ-related cardiotoxicity and acts as guard against TZ-related cardiac impact. The current findings are preliminary and highlight the need for additional studies to answer this current research question.

articles.title: Development of Polymeric Microneedles with Variable Lengths for Delivery of Ebselen in Sporotrichosis.
articles.abstract: Sporotrichosis is a subcutaneous mycosis of public health relevance due to the increased zoonotic transmission associated with felines. Ebselen (EB), a poorly water-soluble organic selenium compound, reacts with thiol groups of redox proteins, increases oxidative stress, and causes fungal death. Microneedles (MN) create microchannels in the skin, disrupting the stratum corneum and allowing the release and diffusion of the drug into deeper layers, potentially reaching blood capillaries. Sporotrichosis is typically treated with intravenous or oral therapies. Thus, this study developed polymeric MN for EB delivery, improving drug incorporation and dispersion while providing a minimally invasive topical alternative. A spectrophotometric method for EB analysis was validated. The molds (long and short microneedles) proved to be transparent, flexible, and easy to remove from the MN. The best formulations (F02, F09, F16, and F17) were selected. EB solubility was 0.15%. In light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), both MN types presented well-defined and intact structures. In the compression test, the best formulation (F17) was selected in both molds. In vitro evaluation of the EB release profile from F17 showed that the long mold formulation released the drug faster than the short mold one. In vitro analysis of antifungal activity showed that the formulation containing EB induced the formation of an inhibitory halo, demonstrating antifungal activity against the fungus Sporothrix brasiliensis. Thus, the current results suggest that the MN containing EB is a promising system. Additional biological studies are required to fully assess their safety and performance in the context of sporotrichosis.

articles.title: Risk-based governance of AI-tools used in health-based exposure limit derivation.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to toxicological assessment and health-based exposure limit (HBEL) derivation, offering potential gains in literature retrieval efficiency, methodological consistency, but introducing novel risks such as hallucinated citations, misattributed findings, and fluent yet scientifically shallow narratives. This article examines AI-assisted HBEL derivation through established HBEL quality framework and clarifies its regulatory expectations. HBEL monographs function as scientific expert assessments that inform GMP risk-management, rather than GxP records, a key distinction that is central to establishing proportionate GMP validation requirements. Building on EMA Annex 11 and draft Annex 22, FDA guidance on AI-supported decision-making, and ICH M7 model qualification principles, the article proposes a tiered, risk-proportionate validation framework. Full computerized system validation is not inherently required for AI tools supporting HBEL derivation. Instead, governance should focus on data limitations, and data source verification. Crucially, experienced human toxicologist review and peer review remain the primary, non-negotiable quality controls, ensuring scientific accountability and materially reducing the validation burden on AI components.

articles.title: Approaches to Enhance the Regenerative Potential of MSC-derived Extracellular Vesicles (MSCEV): A Promising Cell-free Therapy for Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis therapy remains a big challenge since no causative treatment options are available so far. Current preclinical studies report that extracellular vesicles derived from mesenchymal stem cells have high potential to change disease evolution and protect the cartilage matrix. Extracellular vesicles are diverse nanoscale, membrane-bound particles that mediate and regulate intercellular communication. Their therapeutic efficacy in terms of clinical translation is highly dependent on the status of mesenchymal stem cells. Mesenchymal stem cells have been shown to respond to different aspects of the injury microenvironment. Recent research has explored the use of diverse stimuli to enhance stem cell secretion and improve the biological activity of released extracellular vesicles. The most common approach to influence the profile and biological activities of mesenchymal stem cell-derived factors is to recreate a pro-inflammatory environment mimicking an in vivo pathological setting, but other promising methods also deserve to be investigated. This narrative review summarizes and discusses recent strategies aimed at enhancing the regenerative and supportive effect of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles by improving the secretion capacity of cells via different stimulation, with a focus on the development and clinical translation of engineered vesicles for joint disorders. Relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed and Web of Science for peer-reviewed articles published between 2018 and 2026, with priority given to experimental, translational, and clinical studies investigating MSCEVs in OA and approaches for modifying their production, cargo, targeting, or delivery.

articles.title: Identification of Lead Compounds for Pesticides using Computer Aided Drug Discovery.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The agricultural sector heavily relies on pesticides to mitigate the impact of pest infestations. In recent years, Computer-Aided Drug Discovery (CADD) has become popular in the pharmaceutical industry for its cost and time efficiency. The proposed research uses CADD methodologies to identify lead compounds for pesticide development. METHODS: This study focuses on pharmacophore properties and Chemically Advanced Template Search (CATS) descriptors to assess the similarity score against known pesticides. Similarity metrics, including the Tanimoto coefficient and Cosine similarity, were used to ensure precise molecular similarity. The Analysis of Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADME-T) properties, along with physicochemical characteristics, enhances the understanding of newly identified lead compounds. Furthermore, the Hao filter was applied to physicochemical properties to screen pesticide-like compounds. The Hao filter criteria included molecular weight (≤ 435), number of rotatable bonds (≤9), number of hydrogen bond donors (≤2), number of hydrogen bond acceptors (≤ 6), and logP (≤ 6). RESULTS: Subsequently, from the initial pool of 120 lead compounds, 75 compounds were identified as meeting the criteria of the Hao filter, demonstrating their potential as promising pesticide candidates. DISCUSSION: This study underscores the utility of CADD in facilitating the identification and prioritization of potential pesticide candidates. CONCLUSION: The findings provide insights into the integration of computational approaches in agrochemical discovery.

articles.title: Identification of the Proapoptotic Mechanism of Astragalosides in Rheumatoid Arthritis Therapy Based on HPLC, Bioinformatics and Network Pharmacology.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Astragalosides (ASTs), principal active saponins derived from Astragalus, exert prominent therapeutic efficacy against Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA). However, few studies have investigated the molecular mechanism of ASTs in RA therapy. METHODS: AST components were qualitatively and quantitatively analyzed by HPLC. RA-related Differentially Expressed Genes (DEGs) were acquired from the GSE77298 dataset, and AST target genes were predicted via multiple databases. Core hub genes and signaling pathways were screened through bioinformatics analyses, including GO/KEGG enrichment, PPI network and MCODE modularity analysis. Molecular docking was performed to evaluate the binding affinity between ASTs and core apoptotic genes. Cell phenotypic assays, qRT-PCR, Western blot and CASP8 siRNA interference experiments were conducted to validate the regulatory effect of ASTs on the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 axis in MH7A cells. RESULTS: In total, 5781 DEGs were obtained from the GSE77298 dataset, 496 ASTs-related genes were predicted, among which 156 intersected. They were enriched in 3345 significant GO terms and 121 significant KEGG pathways. Bioinformatic and experimental analyses validated that ATM, CASP8, and XIAP mediate AST-induced MH7A cell apoptosis via the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 axis. DISCUSSION: ASTs decrease cellular proliferation and induce apoptosis in MH7A cells. Moreover, ASTs reduced the expression of XIAP and increased the expression of ATM and CASP8 at both the mRNA and protein levels. In addition, ASTs reversed the effects of siRNA-mediated CASP8 silencing on the mRNA expression of CASP3, ATM, and XIAP. CONCLUSION: ASTs can promote apoptosis in MH7A cells, and the underlying mechanism may involve regulation of the CASP8-ATM-XIAP-CASP3 signaling axis.

articles.title: Preclinical Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacodynamic Modeling of Antibody Nanoconjugates for Breast Cancer Treatment.
articles.abstract: Over the past 5 years, the number of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) entering the oncology market has surged. By contrast, the clinical use of immunoliposomes-nanoparticles that also employ antibodies as targeting agents (i.e., antibody-nanoconjugates, ANCs)-has yet to receive approval. One possible reason is the limited understanding of the relationship between ANC exposure and efficacy. To address this gap, we developed a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model for a docetaxel-trastuzumab ANC. PK and PD studies were conducted in MDA-MB-231 tumor-bearing mice, divided into three treatment groups: (i) control, (ii) free docetaxel + free trastuzumab, and (iii) docetaxel-trastuzumab ANCs. PK data were obtained by fluorescence imaging and captured systemic and tumor distribution of ANCs, while PD data were based on tumor growth measurements. The PK model was built using data from the ANC group, and the PD model was developed across all three treatment groups, with a leave-one-out cross validation strategy for predictive evaluation. Treatment schedule simulations were then performed. Using a population nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) approach, the final PK model included a central and a tumor compartment, each with independent elimination rates. Tumor growth dynamics were best described by a reduced Gompertz model coupled with a Simeoni resistance model. This model demonstrated strong predictive performance. Using only data from the first two treatment cycles (4 time points) and Bayesian estimation in the test set, it accurately predicted systemic and tumor ANC concentrations across the subsequent four treatment cycles, with a relative error (RE) below 15%. Prediction precision was further improved (RE < 5%) when data from one additional treatment cycle were incorporated. Similar performance was achieved for PD data, with tumor volume predictions exhibiting RE < 15% and RE < 7.5% when implementing data from two and three treatment cycles, respectively. The model was then applied to simulate alternative treatment schedules. Interestingly, while systemic exposure remained comparable across regimens, every-5-day administration yielded the greatest tumor exposure compared to daily, weekly, and every-35-day dosing (mean ± SD tumor AUC: 55.4 ± 10.9 mg/kg day vs. 47.6 ± 9.38 mg/kg day, 51.4 ± 11.5 mg/kg day, and 44.6 ± 10.0 mg/kg day, respectively, one-way ANOVA, p < 0.001), highlighting the importance of dosing frequency. Overall, these results illustrate how PK/PD modeling can refine intra-tumor PK understanding and support preclinical development of innovative formulations such as ANCs.

articles.title: Retrospective Evaluation of the Association of Hypoalbuminemia With Acute Treatment Outcomes in Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus Aureus Bacteremia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cefazolin and antistaphylococcal penicillins (ASP) are first-line agents for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia. These agents are substantially protein-bound; however, scant data exist evaluating the impact of hypoalbuminemia on microbiologic and patient outcomes for this indication. OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to assess whether hypoalbuminemia is associated with delayed blood culture clearance in patients with MSSA bacteremia being treated with cefazolin or ASPs as definitive therapy. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients admitted for MSSA bacteremia between January 1, 2006 and December 31, 2019, with a serum albumin obtained between the date of an initial positive blood culture result and 72 hours following initiation of definitive therapy with cefazolin or an ASP. The primary outcome was the rate of persistently positive blood cultures, defined as failure to clear blood cultures within 72 hours of definitive therapy initiation. Patients with a serum albumin ≤2.5 g/dL were compared with those with an albumin >2.5 g/dL. Propensity score weighting was used to account for differences in cohort characteristics. RESULTS: A total of 123 patients were included. After propensity score weighting, patients with hypoalbuminemia had a higher rate of persistently positive blood cultures, both in the overall cohort (45.0% vs 13.2%, P < .001) and in the subgroups of cefazolin (33.0% vs 9.1%, P = .015) and ASP (60.1% vs 18.3%, P = .001) when analyzed separately. After propensity weighting in the combined cohort, the length of stay was longer in the hypoalbuminemic cohort, but no differences in mortality were observed. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Hypoalbuminemia was associated with a delayed 72-hour blood culture clearance in patients with MSSA bacteremia treated with either cefazolin or ASPs.

articles.title: Neurotensin modulation of immune and oxido-inflammatory homeostasis targeting TGF-β activated kinase 1/Nuclear factor-kappa βeta pathway: an integrated in vivo and in silico study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurotensin (NTS) is a brain peptide and is known to regulate several brain pathways. Subsequently NTS involvement in psychosis was administered having its promising therapeutic effects as an antipsychotic drug. Therefore, it has been deduced that targeting the NTS system in the regulation of the immune organs would prove to be a productive strategy for developing the novel immune modulatory drugs. OBJECTIVE: The present study elucidated the potential anti-inflammatory properties of NTS receptor 1 (NTSR1) agonist PD149163 (PD) in modulation of immune organs specifically, spleen and thymus investigating the potential immunomodulatory mechanisms targeting NF-κB /TAK1 signaling pathway. METHODS: Swiss albino female mice were randomly grouped: Group I-control, treatment groups- Group II, Group III and Group IV were intraperitoneally exposed with NTSR1-agonist PD low dose/ PD50 (50 µg /kg bw), PD high dose/ PD100 (100 µg /kg bw) and NTSR1-antagonist SR48692 (500 µg /kg bw), respectively for 28 days. Biochemical, hematological, histopathological, and bioinformatics analyses were performed. Differences were considered statistically significant at P < 0.05. RESULTS: The levels of Nuclear factor kappa beta/NF-κB, Tumor necrosis factor- alpha/TNF-α, Interleukine-6/IL-6, Corticosterone/CORT and pro-oxidant, Lipid-peroxidation/LPx were visibly similar to control after the treatment of PD100 as well as PD50 dose however the elevation was observed with the SR. PD100 dose has a prominent effect on the plasma Interleukine-10/IL-10, CORT, NTS levels and tissue anti-oxidants superoxide dismutase/SOD, catalase/CAT as well as positively regulated the hematological and histological parameters, clearly deciphering NTS's immunomodulatory effects. Furthermore, in silico molecular docking analyses showed that PD exhibited high binding affinity with TGF-β activated kinase 1/TAK1 inflammatory protein, indicating inhibition of TAK1/NF-κB downstream signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: NTS receptor 1 analogs might provide a better understanding of the mechanisms by which NTS regulates immune-system and could be further exploited for managing various immune-related disorders.
